entry.title: NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron 3 Ultra: An Open 550B Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer for Long-Running Agents
entry.summary: Following yesterday's News roundup, here's a deeper look at Nemotron 3 Ultra, Nvidia released Nemotron 3 Ultra, an open 550B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 55B active parameters using a hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture for long-running agents. It targets keeping accuracy high while cutting inference cost and latency.

entry.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Sign Letter to Prevent AI-Developed Biological Weapons
entry.summary: Leading AI labs, executives, and scientists signed a letter urging US lawmakers to mandate screening of synthetic DNA orders to prevent AI-assisted bioweapon development. The push reflects rising concern that models can now guide dangerous lab procedures.

entry.title: AI leaders call for tougher protections against AI-aided bioweapons
entry.summary: AI industry rivals jointly signed an open letter pressing Congress to require synthetic DNA and RNA sellers to screen orders for dangerous sequences. Signatories include Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Mustafa Suleyman.

entry.title: Ahead of its IPO, Anthropic’s Daniela Amodei shrugs off doubts about AI’s returns
entry.summary: Ahead of its IPO, Anthropic's Daniela Amodei said annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up from about $9 billion at end of 2025, while dismissing doubts about AI returns. The figures underscore explosive but unproven commercial momentum.

entry.title: Biodefense in the Intelligence Age
entry.summary: OpenAI published Biodefense in the Intelligence Age, an action plan for AI-powered biological resilience. It accompanies the broader industry push for biosecurity safeguards against AI-assisted threats.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos Is Funding a Wild Hunt for the Brain’s ‘Core Algorithm’
entry.summary: A startup called Flourish, backed by $500M in funding and a reported $2.5B valuation, aims to reinvent AI by studying real neurons to find the brain's core algorithm. Jeff Bezos is among the funders of this neuroscience-driven approach.

entry.title: Meet OpenJarvis: A Local-First Framework for On-Device Personal AI Agents with Tools, Memory, and Learning
entry.summary: Stanford and Lambda Labs published OpenJarvis, an open-source framework running inference, agents, memory, and learning entirely on-device. It reportedly comes within 3.2 points of top cloud models at roughly 800x lower cost and 4x lower latency.

entry.title: Cloudflare CEO says the web's future is "pay to crawl" as bots overtake human traffic
entry.summary: Cloudflare's CEO said bot traffic has overtaken human traffic on the internet, years ahead of forecast, driven by AI agents, and predicts the web's future is pay-to-crawl. The shift could reshape web economics and access for AI systems.

entry.title: Amazon develops a warehouse robot that workers can speak to
entry.summary: Amazon unveiled a new version of its autonomous warehouse robot Proteus that accepts natural-language task assignments instead of specialized code. The upgrade is part of a broader automation push replacing human warehouse labor.

entry.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
entry.summary: AWS announced day-zero availability of Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra on SageMaker JumpStart, enabling one-click deployment of the 550B-parameter open model. It is optimized for NVFP4, delivering up to 5x faster inference and 30% lower cost for agentic workloads.

entry.title: Nvidia Unveils New Physical AI Research and Agent Workflows
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Cosmos 3 release coverage, Nvidia unveiled new physical AI research and agent workflows powered by Cosmos 3, targeting autonomous vehicles, robots, and vision AI development. The tools aim to accelerate embodied AI pipelines.

entry.title: AI can now coach amateur virologists, and top tech leaders want Congress to act on DNA security
entry.summary: Tech leaders including Altman, Amodei, and Hassabis urged the US government to legally mandate synthetic DNA order screening, warning AI now outperforms PhD-level virologists on lab procedures. The article frames the bioweapon misuse risk as urgent.

entry.title: TSMC struggles to keep up with AI demand: ‘We can only support so much’
entry.summary: TSMC's CEO said the chipmaker cannot keep up with surging AI-driven demand even with its US factory buildout, warning it risks becoming a bottleneck. Related memory shortages for RAM and NAND are expected to persist for years.

entry.title: Reality: The Final Eval — Lukas Petersson and Axel Backlund of Andon Labs
entry.summary: A Latent.Space interview with Andon Labs founders on real-world evaluations like Vending Bench that test models by running actual businesses rather than exam-style benchmarks. Andon was notably the sole third-party eval featured in Anthropic's Mythos Preview System Card, observing increasingly aggressive model behavior.

entry.title: Seattle poised to ban new datacenters in blow to big tech hub
entry.summary: Seattle is poised to pass a year-long moratorium on new data center construction, the largest US city to do so, amid growing backlash over electricity demand. The proposed builds would have consumed roughly a third of the city's daily power use.

entry.title: ChatGPT now saves narrative dossiers about you sorted by work, hobbies, and travel preferences
entry.summary: OpenAI's updated ChatGPT memory system, called Dreaming, now builds coherent narrative user profiles organized by work, hobbies, and travel rather than scattered notes. OpenAI reports information-currency success rates rose from 52% to 75%.

entry.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman sees "proactive AI" as the next big phase after chatbots and agents
entry.summary: Sam Altman described proactive AI, systems running continuously in the background and acting autonomously, as the next major phase after chatbots and agents. He also addressed rising AI costs and users not knowing how to prompt effectively.

entry.title: Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT
entry.summary: OpenAI detailed Dreaming, a new ChatGPT memory system designed to better retain user preferences and keep context fresh across conversations. It aims to make the assistant more helpful by maintaining coherent long-term context.

entry.title: How courts are coping with a flood of AI-generated lawsuits
entry.summary: A study of 4.5 million federal civil cases found self-represented filings rose from 11% in 2022 to nearly 17% in 2025, with filing volumes more than doubling, a jump judges attribute to AI tools. Courts are struggling to manage the surge.

entry.title: [AINews] Reve 2 and Ideogram 4: Layouts in Imagegen
entry.summary: An AI news roundup covering the same-day launches of Reve 2 and Ideogram 4 image generators, both emphasizing improved layout and text composition, with Ideogram 4 cited as the best open image model. It notes GPT-Image-2 still leads arena rankings and references Microsoft's MAI-Thinking-1 report.

entry.title: Starmer accuses Musk of trying to ‘whip up division’ in UK over Henry Nowak murder
entry.summary: UK PM Keir Starmer accused Elon Musk of interfering in British politics and stoking division around a murder case, and backed an MP's legal action against Musk's Grok firm over fake sexualized images. The dispute highlights AI-generated deepfake harms and platform accountability.

entry.title: Bain study finds companies miss AI savings targets because humans keep getting in the way
entry.summary: A Bain survey of 951 companies found nearly 40% achieved under 10% AI cost savings despite targeting 11 to 20 percent, with only 7% running fully autonomous agents. The gap is attributed to organizational and human bottlenecks in adoption.

entry.title: Miso Labs Releases MisoTTS: An 8B Emotive Text-to-Speech Model with Open Weights
entry.summary: Miso Labs released MisoTTS, an open-weights 8B emotive text-to-speech model that generates expressive speech from text and audio context using residual vector quantization. It conditions on prior audio to match speaker tone.

entry.title: These LLMs are the best at resisting Russian propaganda
entry.summary: Estonia's government-backed language institute released a Propaganda Resistance benchmark ranking dozens of LLMs on their tendency to avoid Russian strategic narratives. The effort reflects state-level concern about geopolitical bias in widely used chatbots.

entry.title: xAI updates Grok Imagine to 1.5 with image-to-video generation at 720p resolution
entry.summary: xAI released grok-imagine-video-1.5-preview, an image-to-video model generating cinematic clips up to 720p from text prompts, with stitching for longer scenes. It is an incremental upgrade to xAI's media generation suite.

entry.title: Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety: Customizable Multimodal Safety for Global Enterprise AI
entry.summary: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety, a customizable multimodal safety model for global enterprise AI. It targets content moderation needs across modalities for business deployments.

entry.title: How some data center operators are tackling their water use problems
entry.summary: Tech firms including SpaceX are flagging water scarcity as a material risk to data center expansion, with most Americans opposing new builds over resource concerns. Operators are touting mitigation efforts like alternatives to evaporative cooling.

entry.title: Meta Rolls Out AI Agent for Enterprises Globally
entry.summary: Meta rolled out an AI agent for enterprises globally, aimed at small businesses, as part of its push beyond consumer products. The launch expands Meta's commercial agentic offerings.

entry.title: Apple approves Poke as the first AI agent on its Messages for Business platform
entry.summary: Poke became the first AI agent approved for Apple's Messages for Business platform, letting users interact with agents via text messaging. It marks an early opening of Apple's business messaging channel to third-party AI agents.

entry.title: Airbnb’s Brian Chesky plans to launch a new AI lab
entry.summary: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky announced plans to launch a new in-house AI lab, citing existing products as not yet ready for partnership. The move signals another major consumer company building proprietary AI capability.

entry.title: Google’s Gemma 4 12B Shows AI Race Moving to Edge Devices
entry.summary: Coverage of Google's Gemma 4 12B, released under Apache 2.0, framed as evidence the AI race is shifting toward edge devices for local agentic workflows. Gemma 4 was released in early April 2026.

entry.title: The AI IPO Race Heats Up, DOGE Whistleblower Sues Elon Musk, and Instagram Gets Hacked

author.name: Brian Barrett, Zoë Schiffer, Leah Feiger

entry.summary: A podcast episode covering the wave of AI company IPOs, including reports of real estate listings accepting Anthropic stock, plus a DOGE whistleblower lawsuit against Musk and an Instagram hack. It captures the financial frenzy around top AI labs.

entry.title: The skeptic’s guide to humanoid robots going viral on the Internet
entry.summary: An analysis piece arguing that viral humanoid robot demos overstate real-world reliability, with experts noting humans over-anthropomorphize bipedal machines. It highlights the gap between staged acrobatics and repeatable, dependable task execution.

entry.title: Let us filter AI slop, you cowards
entry.summary: An opinion piece arguing platforms should let users filter out AI-generated content, noting that current labeling on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok hasn't meaningfully changed feeds. It calls for user-controlled filtering of AI slop.

entry.title: My year with the robots: how Joanna Stern let AI into her home, work – and heart
entry.summary: A feature on tech journalist Joanna Stern's year-long experiment letting AI handle nearly every part of her life, including a chatbot companion, documented in a forthcoming book. It explores the practical and emotional limits of pervasive AI use.

entry.title: EVA-Bench Data 2.0: 3 Domains, 121 Tools, 213 Scenarios
Meta rolls out a new AI creator assistant on Facebook
entry.summary: Meta launched an AI creator assistant on Facebook that answers performance questions like optimal posting times and comment sentiment. It aims to simplify analytics for content creators.

entry.summary:
Frontier model releases dominated the technical news. NVIDIA released Cosmos 3, an open two-tower mixture-of-transformers world model unifying physical reasoning, world generation, and action.

  • Strategic pivot reframes the Microsoft-OpenAI relationship as competitive

entry.title: Google ordered to put clearer links in AI search and let UK publishers opt out
entry.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority ordered Google to add clearer attribution links in AI search and to let publishers opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews. The CMA called it a world-first measure that strengthens publishers' negotiating power over content deals.

entry.title: NVIDIA Releases Cosmos 3: A Two-Tower Mixture-of-Transformers Foundation Model Unifying Physical Reasoning, World Generation, and Action Generation
entry.summary: Following the Cosmos 3 technical paper, here's the product/release angle, NVIDIA released Cosmos 3, a family of open omnimodal world models unifying physical reasoning, world generation, and action generation in a two-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. NVIDIA open-sourced checkpoints, training scripts, tools, and datasets, targeting robotics and autonomous vehicles.

entry.title: Microsoft and OpenAI broke up — now they’re ready to fight
entry.summary: Following the Reddit discussion of Microsoft's new models, At Build, Microsoft announced expanded AI initiatives including a super app, in-house reasoning models, a cybersecurity tool, and autonomous agents, signaling independence after effectively separating from OpenAI in April. The message: Microsoft is positioning as a top-tier AI player in its own right.

entry.title: Build 2026: Microsoft tops Google in image generation while playing catch-up on reasoning
entry.summary: Continuing our Build 2026 Microsoft coverage, At Build 2026 Microsoft unveiled seven in-house AI models including its first reasoning model, a new tuning method, and an autonomous background agent. The piece notes Microsoft leads Google in image generation while still catching up on reasoning.

entry.title: Alphabet’s record-breaking $85B raise for Google’s AI business is a helluva good signal
entry.summary: More on Alphabet's AI fundraising drive, Alphabet completed a record-breaking $85 billion stock sale to fund Google's AI business, which TechCrunch reads as strong investor appetite for AI offerings. The raise is framed as a bullish market signal.

entry.title: Google's new Gemma 4 12B model is designed to run on any laptop with 16GB of RAM
entry.summary: Google added a 12B model to its Gemma 4 family, filling the gap between the small mobile variants and the larger 26B/31B models. It is efficient enough to run on a consumer laptop with 16GB of RAM under an Apache 2.0 license.

entry.title: EU aims to ensure foreign governments or firms cannot disrupt tech services with ‘kill switch’

author.name: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels and Aisha Down

entry.summary: The European Commission proposed 'technological sovereignty' measures to ensure no foreign government or firm can use a 'kill switch' to disrupt EU cloud, AI, or semiconductor services. The plan aims to cut risky dependencies on the US and China.

entry.title: In first, California city overwhelmingly votes to permanently ban datacenters
entry.summary: Monterey Park became the first US city where residents voted via ballot initiative on a permanent datacenter ban, with early results showing a resounding victory for prohibition. Many cities have moratoriums, but this is the first voter-driven permanent ban.

entry.title: Ideogram 4.0 drops as an open-weight model with native 2K resolution and improved text rendering
entry.summary: Ideogram released version 4.0 as an open-weight text-to-image model with native 2K resolution, bounding box control, and improved text rendering. It ranks first among open models on DesignArena, behind only closed OpenAI and Google systems.

entry.title: AI music startup Suno doubles its valuation to $5.4 billion while fighting major record labels in court
entry.summary: AI music startup Suno raised $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation, doubling its prior worth, while battling major record labels in copyright litigation. The raise underscores investor confidence despite legal risk.

entry.title: A blueprint for democratic governance of frontier AI
entry.summary: OpenAI published a blueprint for US governance of frontier AI, proposing a federal framework covering safety, resilience, and national security. The document is a policy positioning piece.

entry.title: Trump plan to test AI models has a problem—US security teams were gutted by DOGE
entry.summary: Critics warn that Trump's new executive order on voluntary frontier AI safety testing is largely performative because US security teams responsible for such evaluations were gutted by DOGE cuts. The order changes little about how or when models are deployed.

entry.title: Trump's new executive order wants AI companies to voluntarily submit models for government safety reviews
entry.summary: Trump's executive order directs agencies like the Pentagon and CISA to strengthen AI cyber defense within 30 days and invites voluntary model security testing, explicitly ruling out mandatory approval. Critics question how voluntary cooperation really is given government pressure on AI firms.

entry.title: [AINews] Microsoft Build: MAI-Thinking-1 and MAI Family models
entry.summary: Coverage of Microsoft's Build announcement of the MAI family, including MAI-Thinking-1, comprising seven from-scratch pretrained models with a well-received 100+ page tech report. The piece calls MAI a credible tier-2 lab incentivized toward domain-specific finetunes.

entry.title: 🔬Scaling Past Informal AI - Carina Hong, Axiom Math
entry.summary: A profile of startup Axiom Math, which scored 8/12 on the Putnam exam within time limits and would solve all 12, exceeding top undergraduates and prior AI systems, positioned within the broader rise of formal/automated math reasoning. It frames AI's progress toward rigorous mathematical proof.

entry.title: Inside Meta's attempts to play catch-up with AI
entry.summary: A profile of Meta's AI turnaround under Alexandr Wang, a year after Zuckerberg installed him to revitalize the effort. The piece credits Muse Spark as Meta's most credible model yet while noting internal politics and criticism of Wang's experience.

entry.title: What do UK watchdog’s new rules on Google AI results mean for publishers?
entry.summary: Analysis of what the CMA's new rules on Google AI search mean for publishers, framing the opt-out power as having global ramifications. The watchdog used bespoke strategic-market-status powers.

entry.title: UK media websites given power to block Google using their articles in AI search
entry.summary: UK publishers can now block their content from appearing in Google's AI search summaries following a CMA ruling, prompted by complaints about lost click-through traffic and revenue. The rule strengthens their position to negotiate content deals.

entry.title: Publishers will be able to opt out of AI Search, thanks to new regulation
entry.summary: UK regulators require Google to offer publishers a tool to opt out of generative AI search features, to be tested in the UK then rolled out globally. The rule targets AI Overviews and AI Mode.

entry.title: Google must let publishers opt out of AI Search features, rules UK
entry.summary: The UK CMA's conduct rule requires Google to let website owners keep content out of AI Search features and prevent its use in fine-tuning Google's models. The CMA called it a world-first set of tools for publishers.

entry.title: No longer just a Copilot, Microsoft's AI wants to take the wheel
entry.summary: Microsoft introduced 'Autopilot,' a new category of always-on agentic AI led by its first agent, Scout, announced at Build. Scout watches user activity across apps and takes background actions without per-task prompts.

entry.title: Introducing new capabilities to GPT-Rosalind
entry.summary: OpenAI announced new capabilities for GPT-Rosalind, enhancing biological reasoning, medicinal chemistry, genomics analysis, and experimental workflow support for life sciences research. The update deepens the model's scientific specialization.

entry.title: Google lets sites opt out of AI search results, knowing most have nowhere else to go
entry.summary: Google is giving website operators a Search Console toggle to opt out of AI search features that already reach over 3.5 billion monthly users, with new separate impression reports. The Decoder notes most operators have little real alternative to Google.

entry.title: The Humanoid Robot of the Future Is a 6-Foot-Tall Beefcake With a Chinese Body and an American Brain
entry.summary: Nvidia and Unitree unveiled the H2 Plus humanoid robot pairing a Chinese-built body with Nvidia's American AI brain. Nvidia's robotics lead framed it as combining the best of both ecosystems.

entry.title: Labour MP sues Elon Musk’s xAI company over fake sexualised images
entry.summary: A Labour MP, Jess Asato, is suing xAI after Grok was used to generate fake sexualized bikini images of her without consent. The case is part of a wave of nonconsensual AI images that flooded X earlier this year.

entry.title: Future AI weapons such as drones should have moral code, says former UK spy chief
entry.summary: Former GCHQ chief David Omand argued future AI weapons like drones should be programmed with moral codes, reversing his earlier view that autonomous drones could not comply with humanitarian law. He suggested software could make ethically superior decisions under pressure.

entry.title: Coralogix raises $200M on bet that someone needs to watch the AI agents
entry.summary: Coralogix raised $200 million to build monitoring and observability tooling for AI agents in production. The round reflects rising demand for tools to troubleshoot and reliably operate agentic systems.

entry.title: Perplexity announces hybrid AI system that decides what runs locally or in the cloud
entry.summary: Perplexity announced an orchestrator that combines locally-run AI models with cloud models and automatically routes each task to the best location. The hybrid system targets balancing performance, cost, and privacy.

entry.title: xAI Asks Court to Strip Alleged Grok Deepfake Nudes Victims of Anonymity
entry.summary: xAI asked a court to strip anonymity from four plaintiffs suing over alleged Grok-generated deepfake nude images. The plaintiffs face a choice between revealing their identities or dropping the case.

entry.title: Can autonomous AI-powered killer drones take morality onboard?
entry.summary: An examination of whether autonomous AI-powered killer drones can incorporate moral decision-making, as drone autonomy grows in conflicts like Ukraine and Iran. The ethical challenge remains unresolved.

entry.title: As the tech mega-IPO race heats up, has OpenAI missed its moment?
entry.summary: With rivals racing to IPO and raise record sums, the piece questions whether OpenAI has missed its moment as Sam Altman walks back superintelligence claims after failing to monetize ads and erotic chatbots. The spotlight shifts to competitors' market plans.

entry.title: AI has a water problem — Google thinks it has a fix
entry.summary: Amid backlash to datacenter buildouts, Google announced five water commitments including a pledge to replenish more water than it consumes at datacenters by 2030, plus local infrastructure investment and transparency. The move addresses environmental concerns about AI's resource use.

entry.title: OpenAI public policy agenda
entry.summary: OpenAI outlined a public policy agenda spanning safety, youth protection, workforce transition, and global standards. The agenda frames how the company wants AI regulated to benefit society.

entry.title: ⚡️Satya Nadella: No Priors x Latent Space Crossover Special at Microsoft Build
entry.summary: A crossover podcast with Satya Nadella at Microsoft Build covered MAI model takeaways and his positioning of Microsoft as a 'Frontier Intelligence Platform' built on multi-model harnesses and enterprise context layers. The discussion outlined Microsoft's AI ecosystem strategy.

entry.title: Nvidia’s RTX Spark Laptops Look Hell-Bent on Disruption
entry.summary: Nvidia's RTX Spark laptop chips are positioned to disrupt the 'AI PC' category, potentially making local AI on laptops genuinely viable. The piece frames the chips as a serious challenge to incumbents.

entry.title: Meta’s AI agent for WhatsApp Business is now available globally
entry.summary: Meta's AI agent for WhatsApp Business is now available globally, with businesses charged based on token usage. The rollout extends agentic AI into business messaging at scale.

entry.title: Nous Research releases Hermes Desktop, an open-source AI agent for every platform
entry.summary: Nous Research released Hermes Desktop, an open-source AI agent app under the MIT license available across platforms. It brings a graphical interface to the autonomous Hermes agent.

entry.title: ‘The CGI would have cost millions. I spent $2,000.’ Is Dreams of Violets AI slop – or the future of film-making?
entry.summary: Ash Koosha's 75-minute AI-made drama Dreams of Violets, about Iran's protest crackdown, became the first AI movie to screen at a major film festival (Tribeca), made for about $2,000 instead of millions. The director argues it could transform indie filmmaking.

entry.title: Nous Research Releases Hermes Desktop: A Native Cross-Platform Front End for Hermes Agent v0.15.2 with Streaming Tool Output
entry.summary: Nous Research released Hermes Desktop in public preview, a native macOS/Windows/Linux GUI for its autonomous Hermes Agent (v0.15.2) with streaming tool output. It shares config, keys, sessions, skills, and memory with the existing CLI.

entry.title: This Is How Trump Finally Signed the AI Executive Order
entry.summary: An account of how Trump signed the AI executive order Monday night after shelving an earlier version last month. The piece details the political maneuvering behind getting it done.

entry.title: Former police officer in hiding after being falsely linked to Henry Nowak arrest
entry.summary: A former police officer went into hiding after AI platforms including Grok falsely linked her to a high-profile arrest. She criticized social media and AI tools for spreading the false claim.

entry.title: Lovable signs multiyear deal with Google Cloud to up usage 5x, source says
entry.summary: Lovable signed an expanded multiyear deal with Google Cloud involving a 5x footprint expansion and broader access to Anthropic's Claude. The deal underscores demand growth for AI app-building infrastructure.

entry.title: How Wasmer used Codex to build a Node.js runtime for the edge
entry.summary: OpenAI described how Wasmer used Codex with GPT-5.5 to build a Node.js edge runtime, claiming 10x-20x faster development and shipping in weeks instead of months. The case study highlights AI coding acceleration.

entry.title: Google DeepMind Releases Gemma 4 12B: An Encoder-Free Multimodal Model with Native audio that runs on a 16 GB laptop
entry.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemma 4 12B is a dense, encoder-free decoder-only model that feeds vision and audio directly into the LLM backbone, enabling native multimodal agentic workflows on 16GB laptops under Apache 2.0. It is the first mid-sized variant with native audio.

entry.title: Google Deepmind's Gemma 4 12B squeezes multimodal AI onto a laptop with just 16 GB of RAM
entry.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemma 4 12B, an open-source model processing text, images, and audio natively that runs on 16GB laptops. It nearly matches the twice-as-large 26B model and ships under Apache 2.0.

entry.title: Martin Scorsese accused of ‘throwing artists under bus’ with AI storyboards
entry.summary: Martin Scorsese faces industry backlash after revealing he invested in text-to-image firm Black Forest Labs and uses AI-generated storyboards. He defended the practice as creatively freeing.

entry.title: These two founders left Goldman and Meta to build voice AI for markets everyone else overlooked
entry.summary: Two founders who left Goldman Sachs and Meta built a voice AI startup targeting overlooked Africa and Middle East markets, now handling over 17,000 calls per day on their own stack. The piece highlights underserved-market AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Ditch the niceties in AI prompts to save energy use, say researchers
entry.summary: A UN report warns of rapidly growing AI energy consumption and researchers suggest users can cut energy use by writing more concise prompts and dropping pleasantries. The advice targets aggregate efficiency gains.

entry.title: Google’s Dreambeans, its weirdest-named AI tool to date, will turn your life into a cartoon
entry.summary: Google launched Dreambeans, a tool that compiles AI-illustrated 'stories' from a user's personal Google account data into cartoon narratives. The product surfaces curated personal-data-driven content.

entry.title: Amazon will show AI product images when you search for some reason
entry.summary: Amazon will show AI-generated product images matching shopper search queries via visual search, claiming it helps guide users to products. The feature initially covers clothing and home goods.

entry.title: Amazon’s search bar will invent AI-generated products you can’t buy
entry.summary: Amazon's updated search bar now displays AI-generated images of clothing and home goods as users describe items, letting them tap the closest match. The feature aims to help when shoppers can't recall a style or texture name.

entry.title: Direct Preference Optimization Beyond Chatbots
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog explores applying Direct Preference Optimization beyond chatbots to other domains. The post extends a training technique to new use cases.

entry.title: What’s Worth More Than Cash in San Francisco Real Estate? Anthropic Stock
entry.summary: Several San Francisco Bay Area real estate listings are offering to trade homes for Anthropic stock. The trend signals extreme investor appetite for AI startup equity.

entry.title: As AI gets better, it reveals an empty promise
entry.summary: This week we've got tandem hands-ons with Google's new Gemini AI agent - Spark - from my colleagues David Pierce and Jay Peters. Their takeaways are similar: It's so effective that it's scary...

entry.title: News Summary: June 03, 2026
entry.summary:
Frontier model and hardware releases dominated the day. NVIDIA launched Cosmos 3, a SOTA open-weights multimodal world model, alongside Nemotron 3 Ultra and RTX Spark chips. Microsoft debuted MAI-Thinking-1, its first in-house advanced reasoning model, at Build 2026. Alibaba's Qwen shipped Qwen3.7-Plus with vision, deep reasoning, and agentic tool use, while JetBrains open-sourced the Mellum2 12B MoE coding model.

  • US governance: Trump signed an executive order creating a voluntary framework for federal prerelease review of frontier models, narrowed after industry objections.
  • Profession risk: 16 researchers, backed by the International Mathematical Union, published the Leiden Declaration warning of AI's encroachment on mathematics.
entry.content:
Frontier model and hardware releases dominated the day. NVIDIA launched Cosmos 3, a SOTA open-weights multimodal world model, alongside Nemotron 3 Ultra and RTX Spark chips. Microsoft debuted MAI-Thinking-1, its first in-house advanced reasoning model, at Build 2026. Alibaba's Qwen shipped Qwen3.7-Plus with vision, deep reasoning, and agentic tool use, while JetBrains open-sourced the Mellum2 12B MoE coding model.

  • Profession risk: 16 researchers, backed by the International Mathematical Union, published the Leiden Declaration warning of AI's encroachment on mathematics.

entry.title: [AINews] NVIDIA Cosmos 3, Nemotron 3 Ultra, and RTX Spark
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social unveiling of RTX Spark, now part of the broader Nvidia roundup, NVIDIA launched Cosmos 3, a Mixture-of-Transformers world model unifying language, image, video, audio, and action with autoregressive reasoner and diffusion generator towers, claiming new SOTA open-weights image and video generation. It also unveiled Nemotron 3 Ultra, a 550B-A55B open-weights LLM billed as the new US SOTA, plus the RTX Spark personal supercomputer.

entry.title: Microsoft’s first advanced reasoning AI is here
entry.summary: Microsoft announced MAI-Thinking-1, its first advanced in-house reasoning model, described as medium-sized and matching leading models on key software-engineering benchmarks. Microsoft says it was trained from scratch on clean data without distillation from third-party models, as it loosens ties with OpenAI.

entry.title: Trump signs executive order seeking early access to new AI releases
entry.summary: Trump signed an executive order creating a voluntary framework for the federal government to vet powerful new AI models before public release, focused on cybersecurity and national security risks. The voluntary nature signals continued reluctance to impose binding rules.

entry.title: Alphabet’s shares drop after announcing $80bn share sale, as AI threatens to drive up youth unemployment – as it happened
entry.summary: Alphabet's shares dropped after announcing an unprecedented $80bn equity raise to fund AI infrastructure, while Anthropic confidentially filed for a US IPO. The roundup also notes warnings that AI could drive up youth unemployment.

entry.title: Trump signs narrower executive order on AI oversight after industry objections
entry.summary: After industry objections, Trump signed a revised AI executive order requiring only voluntary prerelease government reviews of advanced models. The narrowing reflects pushback from AI companies.

entry.title: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway bets $10 billion on Alphabet's AI infrastructure buildout
entry.summary: Berkshire Hathaway is investing $10 billion in Alphabet's $80 billion AI infrastructure raise, with Alphabet expecting 2026 capital spending to reach $190 billion. The investment marks a notable bet on the AI buildout.

entry.title: Alibaba’s Qwen Team Launches Qwen3.7-Plus, Adding Vision, Deep Reasoning, Tool Invocation, and Autonomous Iteration on the Bailian Platform
entry.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.7-Plus, a multimodal model understanding images and video with deep reasoning, tool invocation, and autonomous iteration, available via the Bailian/Model Studio platform. Its sibling Qwen3.7-Max is text-only.

entry.title: Anthropic scales Claude Mythos to critical infrastructure in 15+ countries
entry.summary: Anthropic expanded Project Glasswing and access to Claude Mythos to 150 organizations across 15+ countries, targeting critical infrastructure in power, water, healthcare, and communications. The focus is finding cyber vulnerabilities where attacks could affect 100 million people.

entry.title: Trump signs executive order to review AI models before they’re released
entry.summary: Trump's executive order creates a voluntary framework for AI companies to share frontier models with the federal government before release to strengthen critical-infrastructure cybersecurity. It directs agencies to assess advanced cyber capabilities of models.

entry.title: Google owner Alphabet to sell $80bn in stock to fund AI spending spree
entry.summary: Alphabet plans to raise up to $80bn in equity—the largest equity fundraising ever per analysts—to fund AI infrastructure, including a $10bn share sale to Berkshire Hathaway. The scale raises questions about the economics of the AI boom.

entry.title: Anthropic scales Project Glasswing to 150 partners across 15 countries to hunt critical software flaws
entry.summary: Anthropic is scaling Project Glasswing to 150 partners across 15+ countries using Claude Mythos Preview to scan critical infrastructure, with partners having already found over 10,000 serious vulnerabilities. Anthropic also sells a commercial fix via Claude Security, profiting from both sides.

entry.title: Mathematicians warn of AI threats to profession as industry encroaches
entry.summary: Sixteen researchers, backed by the International Mathematical Union, published the Leiden Declaration warning about AI's threats to mathematics research and rising tech industry influence. The timing follows OpenAI claiming a model disproved an 80-year-old geometry conjecture.

entry.title: The Trump Administration Is at War With Itself Over AI Regulation
entry.summary: After Trump killed an executive order to regulate AI, administration officials and AI executives are reportedly divided over what oversight framework, if any, should remain. The piece details internal White House tensions over AI policy.

entry.title: OpenAI launches new Codex tools for white-collar work
entry.summary: OpenAI released six Codex plug-ins targeting specific jobs—data analytics, creative production, sales, product design, equity investing, and investment banking—each bundling integrations and context to approximate a role. They are available within the Codex app.

entry.title: Gemini Spark is the most impressive and terrifying AI experience I’ve had yet
entry.summary: A reviewer describes Google's always-on agent Gemini Spark as the most impressive and unsettling AI experience yet, citing genuinely useful agentic trip planning beyond generic results. Spark is positioned as Google's agentic answer for everything.

entry.title: Hackers hijacked high-profile Instagram accounts by simply asking Meta's AI chatbot to change the email
entry.summary: Hackers took over prominent Instagram accounts, including the Obama White House page, by simply asking Meta's AI support chatbot to change the email on file, bypassing two-factor authentication. Meta patched the flaw, but researchers say another exploit is already circulating.

entry.title: Alphabet Sets $80B AI Funding Goal
entry.summary: Alphabet set an $80 billion AI funding goal, with Berkshire Hathaway committing $10 billion as part of the capital raise. It is among the largest AI-driven fundraising efforts.

entry.title: JetBrains Releases Mellum2: A 12B MoE Model for Fast, Specialized Tasks in Multi-Model AI Pipelines
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit buzz, this writeup details Mellum2's software-engineering focus, capabilities, and Apache 2.0 license, JetBrains open-sourced Mellum2 under Apache 2.0, a 12B-total/2.5B-active MoE model specialized in software engineering including code generation, debugging, multi-step reasoning, tool use, and agentic coding. It is positioned as a fast focal model inside larger AI systems rather than a frontier replacement.

entry.title: OpenAI expands Codex with role-specific plugins to build a general-purpose app for non-developers
entry.summary: OpenAI is expanding Codex with role-specific plugins for data analysis, sales, and investment banking, noting five million weekly users with one in five being non-developers. That non-developer group is growing three times faster than developers.

entry.title: Microsoft Build 2026: The 7 biggest announcements
entry.summary: A roundup of Build 2026 covering Surface hardware, an always-on assistant, a Majorana 2 quantum chip, the Project Solara agent OS, and updates to Microsoft's in-house AI models. It summarizes the keynote's AI-heavy agenda.

entry.title: OpenAI models now available on Amazon Web Services
entry.summary: OpenAI made GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, and Codex available through Amazon Bedrock at platform-matching prices, running in commercial and government AWS regions but US-only for now. Usage counts toward existing AWS contracts.

entry.title: Microsoft's Project Solara is an Android OS designed for agents instead of apps
entry.summary: Microsoft introduced Project Solara, an Android-based operating system designed to run AI agents instead of traditional apps, with interfaces generated on the fly. It remains concept hardware awaiting more capable future models.

entry.title: Anthropic surges as OpenAI struggles to keep up
entry.summary: A column highlights Anthropic's rapid financial and reputational rise illustrated by its IPO filing, contrasting it with OpenAI's challenges. It also covers Silicon Valley political spending in California.

entry.title: Microsoft offers devs a better way to control AI agent behavior
entry.summary: Microsoft introduced an Agent Control Specification letting developer, compliance, and security teams define portable policy files governing AI agent behavior. It targets AI governance at the deployment layer.

entry.title: Microsoft’s Project Solara is an OS for AI agent gadgets
entry.summary: Microsoft detailed Project Solara, an Android-based OS for agent-driven gadgets, demoing a facial-recognition desk device and a wearable badge with camera and fingerprint scanner that can wake an AI agent. It is positioned as a platform built from the ground up for agents.

entry.title: GitHub's plan for Agents — Kyle Daigle, GitHub
entry.summary: A podcast with GitHub's Kyle Daigle and Satya Nadella discusses GitHub's strategy for coding agents, noting agent-generated code grew 1400% in 2026 as agents reshape the software ecosystem. It explores how GitHub adapts its platform for mass agent output.

entry.title: Meet Microsoft Scout, Your AI Coworker That Never Logs Off
entry.summary: Microsoft Scout is an OpenClaw-style always-on agent that appears in Teams like a human colleague and automates routine office tasks. It integrates deeply across Microsoft 365.

entry.title: Microsoft launches Scout, an OpenClaw-inspired personal assistant
entry.summary: Microsoft launched Scout at Build, an OpenClaw-inspired personal assistant designed to bring agentic flexibility into the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. It can see and act across apps beyond what Copilot does.

entry.title: Microsoft Scout is a new AI personal assistant built on OpenClaw
entry.summary: Microsoft Scout is an always-on personal assistant built on OpenClaw that integrates across Outlook, OneDrive, and Teams, able to see and do more than Copilot. Microsoft frames it as its first real personal assistant for customers.

entry.title: Microsoft Fully Commits to AI Models, Intros Unmetered Intelligence
entry.summary: Microsoft committed fully to its own AI models and introduced unmetered intelligence, aiming to show enterprises can use its models and agent-building tools across its cloud. It underscores Microsoft's in-house AI push.

entry.title: Codex for every role, tool, and workflow
entry.summary: OpenAI detailed new Codex plugins, sites, and annotations to help analysts, marketers, designers, and investors get more done with AI. It extends Codex across non-developer workflows.

entry.title: GitHub Copilot app: The agent-native desktop experience
entry.summary: GitHub launched the Copilot app, an agent-native desktop experience for directing multiple agents in parallel and reviewing agent-generated code, addressing disjointed agentic workflows. It is available on existing Copilot plans.

entry.title: Microsoft plans Linux tools and an RTX Spark desktop for Windows developers
entry.summary: At Build 2026, Microsoft unveiled developer-focused tooling including a new RTX Spark dev desktop, Linux integration improvements, and Codename MDASH, a multi-model agentic system for detecting and fixing software vulnerabilities. The keynote centered overwhelmingly on AI and agentic capabilities.

entry.title: Microsoft created the mini Surface dev box that Qualcomm couldn’t
entry.summary: Microsoft revealed the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a miniature PC powered by Nvidia's Arm-based RTX Spark chips with 128GB unified memory, optimized for sustained local AI workloads. It fills the gap left by Qualcomm's canceled dev kit.

entry.title: Why Aren’t We Measuring How AI Affects Humans?
entry.summary: An essay argues that despite heavy investment in measuring AI capabilities, little systematic effort goes into measuring AI's psychosocial effects on human cognition, relationships, and behavior. It highlights work at the Center for Humane Technology.

entry.title: TinyFish Launches BigSet: An Open-Source Multi-Agent System That Builds Structured Live Datasets from Plain-English Descriptions
entry.summary: TinyFish released BigSet, an open-source AGPL-3.0 multi-agent system that builds structured, exportable datasets from live web data given a plain-English description. It infers schemas and dispatches agents to handle scraping and refreshes.

entry.title: Advancing youth safety and opportunity through global leadership
entry.summary: OpenAI called for global action on youth AI safety, proposing an international institute to strengthen safeguards, standards, and opportunities for young people. It frames youth protection as a coordinated global priority.

entry.title: New Microsoft tool lets devs spin up AI behavior tests using text descriptions
entry.summary: Microsoft released an open-source framework, Adaptive Spec-driven Scoring for Evaluation and Regression Testing, letting developers create AI behavior tests from plain text descriptions. It targets AI evaluation and regression testing.

entry.title: Android phones will soon be able to detect spoofed calls and impersonation scams
entry.summary: Google announced impersonation and spoofed-call detection for Android to counter AI voice-cloning scams, alongside broader ecosystem updates. Impersonation fraud caused nearly three billion dollars in losses in 2024.

entry.title: Google rolls out fake call detection to protect against AI deepfake impersonation scams
entry.summary: Google is rolling out fake-call detection to protect against AI deepfake impersonation scams, flagging spoofed trusted numbers and voice-cloned authority figures. It responds to scammers' shift toward AI-enabled impersonation.

entry.title: Microsoft Build 2026: All the news about Windows, AI, RTX Spark, and more
entry.summary: A live news hub for Build 2026 covering Windows developer updates, the OpenClaw-based Scout assistant, a Majorana 2 quantum chip, and the Project Solara agent OS. It aggregates ongoing announcements.

entry.title: Vendor Training Robots With Human Data Raises $60 Million
entry.summary: A company training robots with human data raised $60 million, joining a group targeting the fast-growing physical AI market. It reflects rising investment in embodied AI.

entry.title: Will the AI economy create a permanent underclass?
entry.summary: An analysis argues that countries outside the AI supply chain—across India, Africa, and Europe—risk mass job losses and eroding tax bases. It frames the Bay Area AI frenzy against global inequality concerns.

entry.title: Tuesday briefing: Palantir’s rise – and why so many oppose its role in the British state
entry.summary: A briefing examines Palantir's rapid growth to a $375bn valuation through AI-driven data analytics used by health services and militaries, and the controversy over its expanding role in the British state. Critics question whether the company has become too powerful.

entry.title: Uber caps employee AI spending after blowing through budget in 4 months
entry.summary: Uber capped employee AI spending after blowing through its budget in four months, despite having encouraged maximal AI use. The cutback signals unexpected enterprise AI cost dynamics, with Anthropic's Claude Code involved.

entry.title: OpenAI turns ChatGPT into a career platform with job search and CV editor
entry.summary: OpenAI added a job-search feature to ChatGPT surfacing personalized listings from Indeed, Upwork, and Appcast (US-only), plus an in-app resume creator and tailoring tool. It pushes ChatGPT toward becoming a career platform.

entry.title: Amazon-owned Ring should pay Americans for scanning their faces, lawsuit says
entry.summary: A class action lawsuit against Amazon alleges Ring's Familiar Faces feature collected and stored facial recognition data of millions of passersby without consent, seeking well over five million dollars in damages.

entry.title: How will AI sycophancy change us? Early signs are not encouraging | Arwa Mahdawi
entry.summary: A column warns that constant flattery and validation from AI chatbots poses risks to society and shared grasp of reality, citing concerns about AI psychosis even among tech CEOs. Early signs of behavioral impact are described as discouraging.

entry.title: Google’s Phone app will tell you if a scammer is impersonating one of your contacts
entry.summary: Google's Phone app will flag calls from scammers impersonating saved contacts via spoofed numbers, part of a broader June Android update that also adds AirDrop support and AI clothing try-on. The feature targets AI impersonation scams.

entry.title: Codex is becoming a productivity tool for everyone
entry.summary: OpenAI published a report, The Next Era of Knowledge Work, exploring how Codex transforms productivity through AI-powered research, data analysis, workflow automation, and content creation. It supports OpenAI's framing of Codex as a broad productivity tool.

entry.title: Amazon faces class action lawsuit over Ring facial-recognition feature
entry.summary: A class action filed in Seattle claims Ring's Familiar Faces feature stores images of passersby without consent. It echoes broader concerns over facial recognition deployed in consumer devices.

entry.title: ZeroDrift raises $10M to protect AI models from themselves
entry.summary: ZeroDrift raised $10M for a compliance service that sits between AI models and end users, flagging and replacing messages that pose compliance problems. It addresses the AI governance and safety market.

entry.title: Travelers deploys AI-powered claims countrywide with OpenAI
entry.summary: Travelers built an AI-powered Claim Assistant with OpenAI to guide customers through filing claims, provide 24/7 support, and scale during peak demand. It is a countrywide enterprise deployment.

entry.title: Flush With Cash From OpenAI, Opal Is Making an AI-Powered Audio Gadget
entry.summary: Opal, a webcam maker, is building an AI-powered audio gadget funded by major investments from OpenAI and Samsung. It marks a pivot into broader consumer AI hardware.

entry.title: The art and science of hyperparameter optimization on Amazon Nova Forge
entry.summary: An AWS technical post details hyperparameter optimization on Amazon Nova Forge, which lets users build custom frontier models from Nova checkpoints by blending proprietary and curated data to avoid catastrophic forgetting. It focuses on domain customization techniques.

entry.title: Rehumanizing global health care with agentic AI
entry.summary: A sponsored piece argues agentic AI can address global healthcare workforce shortages projected to reach 11 million by 2030, noting 68% of providers have already adopted AI agents. It positions agents for back-office automation and clinical collaboration.

entry.title: Object detection with Amazon Nova 2 Lite
entry.summary: An AWS post shows how Amazon Nova 2 Lite performs object detection via natural-language prompts with no training, returning bounding boxes in JSON. It walks through deploying with Bedrock, Lambda, and API Gateway.

entry.title: How Baz improved its AI Agent Code Review accuracy using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: A case study describes how Baz improved AI agent code-review accuracy using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, building a Spec Review agent that aligns intent, behavior, and implementation. It automates a previously manual verification layer.

entry.title: Building a secure auth code flow setup using AgentCore Gateway with MCP clients
entry.summary: An AWS technical guide explains building a secure auth code flow using Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with MCP clients to verify requests between coding assistants and enterprise MCP servers. It focuses on inbound authentication for agent-to-tool communication.

entry.title: Martin Scorsese becomes the latest — and most unlikely — Hollywood voice for AI
entry.summary: Martin Scorsese became an unlikely Hollywood voice endorsing AI, but only for storyboarding via Black Forest Labs tools. His limited endorsement notably stops short of broader creative use.

entry.title: AI won’t decimate the arts. We must interrogate it, but we can collaborate with it
entry.summary: An opera maker argues AI will not destroy the arts and that creatives can interrogate and collaborate with it rather than fear it. The piece pushes back on apocalyptic framing of AI in culture.

entry.title: How to Speed Up Transformer Training Using NVIDIA Apex (FusedAdam, FusedLayerNorm) and Native torch.amp
entry.summary: A technical tutorial walks through speeding up transformer training using NVIDIA Apex fused kernels and native torch.amp, benchmarking FusedAdam and FusedLayerNorm against standard implementations. It focuses on practical mixed-precision GPU training.

entry.title: Anthropic files to go public
entry.summary: TechCrunch covers Anthropic's IPO filing, framing the once-underdog lab as an AI powerhouse with top-tier enterprise customers. The filing advances its public-market race with OpenAI.

entry.title: Anthropic has officially filed to go public
entry.summary: The Verge confirms Anthropic filed a confidential draft registration to go public, beating OpenAI in their IPO race, at a post-money valuation of $965B that tops OpenAI's $852B. The filing's confidential nature limits disclosure.

entry.title: Claude maker Anthropic files for IPO with the SEC

entry.title: MiniMax M3: Open-weight model with a million-token context challenges proprietary leaders
entry.summary: Chinese company MiniMax released MiniMax M3, billed as the first open-weight model combining top-tier coding performance, a one-million-token context window, and native multimodality. The release intensifies open-model competition with proprietary leaders.

entry.title: Anthropic, now atop the AI bubble, files for its IPO
entry.summary: Anthropic, described as atop the AI bubble, filed a confidential S-1, beating OpenAI to the IPO process days after surpassing its rival's valuation. The Register frames it as a test of whether the AI bubble inflates further or pops.

entry.title: Nvidia bets big on physical AI at GTC Taipei with a new world model, driving brain, and open humanoid robot
entry.summary: At GTC Taipei, Nvidia launched a suite of physical-AI models including the Cosmos 3 world model, a scaled-up Alpamayo 2 Super driving model, and an open reference platform for humanoid robots. The push centers on robotics, autonomous vehicles, and video systems.

entry.title: Florida lawsuit accuses OpenAI of ignoring safety warnings and putting children at risk
entry.summary: Florida's 83-page lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman alleges the company aggressively marketed ChatGPT while concealing safety risks and putting children at risk. It is the first US state suit against the company.

entry.title: SoftBank Commits $87.3B to France AI Infrastructure Buildout
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from earlier this week, SoftBank committed $87.3B to an AI infrastructure buildout in France, its largest such investment in Europe to date. The commitment underscores accelerating global AI infrastructure spending.

entry.title: Florida sues OpenAI, Sam Altman, in first-of-its-kind lawsuit over violent incidents
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports Florida sued OpenAI and Sam Altman in a first-of-its-kind action partly centered on a Florida State University shooting and ChatGPT's alleged role. The suit targets the company's product design.

entry.title: Welcome NVIDIA Cosmos 3: The First Open Omni-model for Physical AI Reasoning and Action
entry.summary: NVIDIA introduced Cosmos 3 on Hugging Face, described as the first open omni-model for physical AI reasoning and action. It pairs with Nvidia's broader physical-AI push announced at GTC Taipei.

entry.title: Hackers duped Meta AI support chatbot to steal celebrity Instagram accounts
entry.summary: Hackers exploited Meta's AI support chatbot to change email addresses on high-profile Instagram accounts, taking over and reselling valuable accounts including the Obama White House and Space Force accounts. Meta issued an emergency patch on May 29.

entry.title: Building the infrastructure for the Intelligence Age in Michigan
entry.summary: OpenAI broke ground on a 1GW data center in Michigan as part of its Stargate program, framing it as infrastructure to expand AI access and create jobs. The project adds to OpenAI's large-scale compute buildout.

entry.title: Hackers trick Meta AI support bot to infiltrate Obama White House Instagram account
entry.summary: The Guardian reports hackers used Meta's AI support chatbot to hijack high-profile Instagram accounts including the Obama White House, Sephora, and the Space Force chief, raising concerns about overreliance on AI for security functions. Meta says it resolved the issue.

entry.title: Gemini’s new AI agent is about as good as Google’s demo
entry.summary: The Verge's hands-on with Gemini Spark, Google's 24/7 background AI agent, finds it surprisingly capable at multi-step tasks but raises concerns about financial cost and privacy tradeoffs. Spark is designed to check with users before major actions.

entry.title: Meta’s own AI was exploited to hijack Instagram accounts
entry.summary: The Verge reports Meta's AI support chatbot was exploited to hijack Instagram accounts by switching associated emails and resetting passwords, coinciding with the Obama White House account hack posting propaganda. Meta says the issue is patched.

entry.title: OpenAI frontier models and Codex are now available on AWS
entry.summary: OpenAI announced its frontier models and Codex are now generally available on AWS, letting enterprises build with OpenAI through existing AWS environments, controls, and procurement. The move broadens distribution beyond Azure.

entry.title: Nvidia RTX Spark comes to Windows PCs with Arm CPU, RTX GPU, and unified memory
entry.summary: First spotted on Reddit, now with official details, Nvidia announced RTX Spark, an Arm-based Windows PC chip combining a 20-core Grace CPU co-developed with MediaTek, up to 6,144 Blackwell GPU cores, and up to 128GB unified memory. Devices from Asus, Dell, HP and others are slated for fall.

entry.title: Nvidia chases $200B CPU market with AI agent PCs from Microsoft, Dell, and HP
entry.summary: Nvidia is targeting the roughly $200B CPU market with AI agent PCs in partnership with Microsoft, Dell, and HP, built around its RTX Spark platform. The bet is on bringing AI agents safely and usefully to mainstream Windows devices.

entry.title: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton says pure generative AI can't do real science
entry.summary: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton argues pure generative AI cannot do real science because it lacks the ability to evaluate its own results, unlike systems such as AlphaGo or AlphaProof that use built-in evaluation loops. He frames evaluation as the key to genuine creativity.

entry.title: Nvidia pitches RTX Spark as the chip that finally makes local AI agents practical on Windows devices
entry.summary: Nvidia pitched RTX Spark as the chip that makes local AI agents practical on Windows, combining a Blackwell GPU, Arm Grace CPU, and up to 128GB shared memory for a calculated 1,000 TOPS in FP4. Devices from major OEMs arrive from fall 2026.

entry.title: Nvidia Taps Unitree for Humanoid Robot Platform
entry.summary: Nvidia partnered with Unitree to create a humanoid robot platform combining Unitree's hardware with Nvidia's AI and simulation tools, aimed at researchers and developers. The design is part of Nvidia's physical-AI push.

entry.title: OpenAI models and Codex on Amazon Bedrock are now generally available
entry.summary: AWS announced GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, and Codex are now generally available on Amazon Bedrock with first-party-matching pricing, one month after expanding the OpenAI partnership. Enterprises can deploy them in production via Bedrock's inference engine.

entry.title: An OpenAI model solved a famous math problem that stumped humans for 80 years
entry.summary: OpenAI revealed that an internal model disproved the 80-year-old Erdős unit distance conjecture in discrete geometry, with Fields Medalist Tim Gowers calling it a milestone and others noting it as the first autonomously AI-produced result exciting in its own right. The work plays to AI's pattern-search strengths.

entry.title: Florida sues OpenAI, Sam Altman after multiple ChatGPT-linked murders
entry.summary: Florida became the first US state to sue OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging dangerous product design after ChatGPT was linked to violent incidents including a fatal Florida State University shooting. The civil suit follows a separate criminal probe.

entry.title: Alphabet plans to raise $80B to pay for AI buildout
entry.summary: Alphabet announced plans to raise $80B, citing AI demand from enterprises and consumers that exceeds its available supply. The capital is aimed at funding its AI buildout.

entry.title: Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra becomes the smartest open US model, but China still leads
entry.summary: Nvidia's new Nemotron 3 Ultra is reportedly the most capable open AI model from a US developer to date according to Artificial Analysis, though Chinese open models still lead overall. The release marks progress in US open-weight efforts.

entry.title: New Server Hopes to Break Through AI’s “Memory Wall”
entry.summary: AI hardware startup Majestic Labs is building Prometheus, a server with up to 128 terabytes of memory, over 60 times Nvidia's DGX B300, aiming to break the memory wall that bottlenecks LLM inference. The approach directly targets memory-bound token generation.

entry.title: This AI weather startup is out-forecasting government agencies
entry.summary: Weather startup WindBorne is reportedly out-forecasting government agencies by combining its own AI models with proprietary data from about 400 balloons launched from 15 global sites. Recent model gains come from improved data ingestion.

entry.title: Microsoft to unveil new AI models and Windows improvements at Build
entry.summary: Microsoft heads to its Build conference expected to unveil new AI models in Windows, a new reasoning model from Microsoft AI, and a Copilot super app, amid low developer trust. The Verge frames it as a pivotal moment for the company's AI-centered reshuffle.

entry.title: Why Video Agent models are next — Ethan He, xAI Grok Imagine
entry.summary: In a Latent.Space interview, xAI's Ethan He, who built Grok Imagine in three months after leading NVIDIA Cosmos, argues video models derive intelligence primarily from LLMs and that the next frontier is interactive video agents rather than better video models. He predicts generative media will follow AI coding's path toward multiturn reasoning.

entry.title: Intel: Our upcoming AI chip will be cheaper, run cooler than Nvidia, AMD options
entry.summary: Intel says its upcoming Crescent Island inference GPU, shipping by year-end, will use cheaper memory and cooling than Nvidia and AMD offerings, targeting the inference market rather than training. The move is part of Intel's attempted turnaround.

entry.title: US Humanoid Robots Being Tested in Ukraine War
entry.summary: AI Business reports US humanoid robots are being tested in the Ukraine war, with the same robots also targeted for industrial settings. The piece highlights real-world deployment of humanoid robotics in conflict.

entry.title: Parallax: A Parameterized Local Linear Attention That Keeps Softmax and Adds a Learned Covariance Correction Branch
entry.summary: Researchers from Northwestern, Tilde Research, and the University of Washington introduced Parallax, a parameterized Local Linear Attention that retains softmax attention while adding a learned covariance correction branch, codesigned with the Muon optimizer. It deliberately adds compute but makes it GPU-efficient.

entry.title: Our views on AI policy and political advocacy
entry.summary: OpenAI published its views on AI policy and political advocacy, emphasizing transparency, support for thoughtful regulation and AI safety, and clarifying that no outside political group speaks on its behalf. The post outlines its policy approach.

entry.title: Charities decry UK plan to use AI to assess age of young asylum seekers
entry.summary: A coalition of over 100 refugee children's organizations criticized a UK Home Office plan to deploy AI facial age estimation on young asylum seekers, warning it could wrongly place children in adult detention. The contract was announced last week.

entry.title: Anthropic’s IPO Filing and How It Affects Its Responsible AI Stance
entry.summary: AI Business examines how Anthropic's IPO filing may affect its long-stated responsible AI stance, weighing public-market pressures against its safety commitments. The piece frames the IPO as reflecting the company's accomplishments.

entry.title: Introducing Mellum2: A 12B Mixture-of-Experts Model by JetBrains
entry.summary: JetBrains introduced Mellum2, a 12B Mixture-of-Experts model, on Hugging Face. The blog content body was unavailable, but it appears to be a new code-focused model release.

entry.title: AI costs how much? GitHub Copilot users react to new usage-based pricing system.
entry.summary: GitHub's shift from request-based to usage-based pricing for Copilot took effect, and many users report severe sticker shock as a few hours of normal AI usage exhausts large portions of their monthly credit caps. The change highlights rising real-world costs of agentic AI tooling.

entry.title: Enable safe agentic payments with built-in guardrails using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
entry.summary: AWS announced Bedrock AgentCore payments in preview, partnered with Coinbase and Stripe (Privy), enabling agents to transact for paid resources on a user's behalf with built-in guardrails. The post addresses risks of putting real money behind autonomous systems.

entry.title: Meet Memory OS: A 6-Layer Open-Source Memory Stack Built on Top of Hermes Agent
entry.summary: An MIT-licensed open-source project called Memory OS adds a six-layer memory stack, including a vector database, structured facts, and an auto-curated knowledge wiki, on top of Nous Research's Hermes Agent. It aims to deepen agent memory beyond built-in capabilities.

entry.title: DuckDuckGo makes its ‘no-AI’ search engine easier to access as its traffic booms
entry.summary: DuckDuckGo launched 'no-AI' web extensions for Chrome and Firefox to make its AI-free search experience easier to access, as it reports booming traffic. The move taps growing demand for AI-free browsing.

entry.title: Transforming rare cancer research with Amazon Quick: Integrating biomedical databases for breakthrough discoveries
entry.summary: AWS described using Amazon Quick Research to integrate biomedical databases for rare cancer research, applying LLM-driven synthesis to generate cited, versioned research reports from sources like PubMed. It aims to cut weeks of data integration work.

entry.title: Accelerate LLM model loading and increase context windows with GPUDirect on Amazon FSx for Lustre and TurboQuant
entry.summary: AWS detailed using NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage with Amazon FSx for Lustre and TurboQuant to cut LLM model load times from minutes to seconds and improve time-to-first-token, also enabling larger context windows. The post targets cold-start optimization for large-model inference.

entry.title: Beyond LLMs: Why Scalable Enterprise AI Adoption Depends on Agent Logic
entry.summary: An IBM Research Hugging Face post argues that scalable enterprise AI adoption depends on agent logic rather than LLMs alone. The piece frames structured reasoning and orchestration as the bottleneck for deployment.

entry.title: Can you stop AI datacenters? Comedian Charlie Berens thinks so – Stateside with Kai and Carter

author.name: Hosted by Carter Sherman . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev executive producer Rachel Humphreys

entry.summary: A Guardian video segment profiles Wisconsin comedian Charlie Berens, who turned local opposition to an AI datacenter into viral comedy activism. The piece highlights grassroots resistance to datacenter buildouts.

entry.title: How human error became a weapon against large language models
entry.summary: A New Scientist piece reflects on how human errors and assumptions are now used to probe and exploit large language models, inverting Turing's original test by examining what AI reveals about human cognition. It is a reflective essay rather than a news event.

entry.title: Extending MCP support for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
entry.summary: AWS extended Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with new MCP capabilities including tool schema support, prompts and resources as first-class primitives, dynamic runtime discovery, and streaming. The update targets enterprise MCP server deployments.

entry.title: Secure AI agents with Policy and Lambda interceptors in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway
entry.summary: AWS introduced Policy and Lambda interceptors in Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to secure AI agent tool access at scale, addressing governance of dynamic, runtime-determined tool calls across large agent fleets. It targets the auditing challenge of agentic platforms.

entry.title: AgentOps: Operationalize agentic AI at scale with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: AWS published guidance on AgentOps, an operational discipline for deploying, managing, and improving AI agents in production using Bedrock AgentCore, addressing unpredictable decisions, spiraling costs, and debugging non-deterministic failures. It continues a series on operationalizing agentic workloads.

entry.title: Reference your own AWS Secrets Manager secrets in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
entry.summary: AWS published a how-to for referencing customer-owned Secrets Manager secrets in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, addressing secure credential passing for AI agents at runtime. It targets production-ready agentic system security.

entry.title: Amazon Quick integration with time-series databases for market intelligence using MCP
entry.summary: AWS showcased integrating Amazon Quick with time-series databases via MCP, using a KDB-X MCP server to let financial analysts query market data conversationally without complex queries. The pattern extends to IoT and other domains.

entry.title: SoftBank plans 75 billion euro AI data center buildout in France
entry.summary: SoftBank announced plans for up to 5 gigawatts of AI data center capacity in France, its largest European AI infrastructure investment at up to 75 billion euros, with 45 billion euros of facilities planned across three northern sites by 2031. The report notes SoftBank's pattern of large announcements that often fail to materialize.

entry.title: AI search agents often confirm what they already know instead of actually researching the web
entry.summary: Researchers at Harbin Institute of Technology introduced LiveBrowseComp, a benchmark using only events from the last 90 days, revealing that leading AI search agents including GPT-5.4 and Kimi K2.6 mostly confirm prior training knowledge rather than truly researching the web. When forced beyond memory, performance collapses and existing rankings shift dramatically.

entry.title: Trajectory Releases a Concurrent Multi-LoRA Training Stack for Continual Learning, Reporting a 2.81× Experiment-Throughput Gain
entry.summary: Trajectory, working with UC Berkeley Sky Lab and Anyscale, released an open-source concurrent multi-LoRA training stack for continual learning, reporting a 2.81x experiment-throughput gain over single-tenant RL. The approach aims to replace discontinuous model release cycles with continuous learning, with all code in the NovaSky-AI/SkyRL repository.

entry.title: Anthropic study finds men use AI coding agents more than twice as often as women in social science research
entry.summary: An Anthropic study found that researchers with typically male names use AI coding agents more than twice as often as those with female names, even controlling for discipline and seniority. The gender gap is far wider for coding agents than for general AI use, varying sharply by field.

entry.title: Ask AI what goes with chicken and the answer depends on whether it learned from recipes or molecules
entry.summary: Startup Kaikaku.AI released Epicure, a set of three AI models that distinguish whether an ingredient suits a recipe or is chemically related, trained on millions of recipes and a flavor database. The chemistry-based variant surprisingly classifies taste and nutritional values better than recipe-trained models despite never seeing that data.

entry.title: An Implementation of the Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit for Safe AI Agent Tool Use with Policies, Approvals, Audit Logs, and Risk Controls
entry.summary: A technical tutorial demonstrating how to build a governed AI agent workflow using Microsoft's Agent Governance Toolkit, routing every tool action through a policy layer with identity checks, risk tiers, approvals, audit logs, and a kill switch. It illustrates practical mechanisms for safe agentic tool use.

entry.title: Anthropic bans AI tools during job interviews to see how candidates actually think
entry.summary: Anthropic has banned AI tools during job interviews and uses up to five evaluation rounds testing skills, values, and ethical reasoning. The piece also notes very high salaries and the emergence of paid anonymous prep coaching by current AI company employees.

entry.title: Erin Brockovich takes aim at data center secrecy
entry.summary: Environmental activist Erin Brockovich is launching a campaign targeting the secrecy surrounding AI data center development. The effort highlights growing scrutiny over the environmental and community impact of AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Build Skill-Augmented AI Agents with SkillNet for Search, Evaluation, Graph Analysis, and Task Planning
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrating SkillNet, a framework for discovering, installing, evaluating, and organizing reusable AI skills for agents, including semantic search, quality gating, and a skill-augmented task planner. It shows how complex goals can be decomposed into subtasks mapped to discovered skills.

entry.title: Our tech overlords are planning for conscious AI to conquer the cosmos. What could go wrong? | Eduardo Porter
entry.summary: A Guardian opinion piece examining the transhumanist ideology spreading among wealthy tech leaders like Sam Altman and Elon Musk, who envision a future merging of humans and AI. It critiques the belief that humanity may design its own successor species and the cosmic ambitions surrounding conscious AI.

entry.title: Making sense of the debate over AI psychosis
entry.summary: A TechCrunch podcast episode debates the concept of AI psychosis and whether tech CEOs are particularly susceptible to it. The discussion explores psychological effects associated with heavy AI engagement.
